name: Ylt

features.Boss: Ylt can take both a fast turn and a slow turn each round. After an enemy finishes a turn, Ylt can spend 1 focus to immediately use an extra ► or ▷. Additionally, he can spend 1 focus on his turn to remove a condition from himself.
features.Flowing Earth: After Ylt uses the Cohesion surge, he can immediately use Vaulting Stone on himself (no action or Investiture required), but it doesn’t grant an advantage on his next attack.
features.Taln’s Honorblade: Ylt is bonded to the Honorblade of the Herald Taln. If he loses the weapon, he can summon it as ►, and it reappears in his hand at the start of his next fast turn. While not wielding it, he can’t use the Cohesion and Tension surges (including Vaulting Stone, Stone Spear, and Tension Parry).

Strike: Honorblade.Description: Attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. Graze: 11 (2d10) spirit damage. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) spirit damage.

Stone Spear.Description: Cohesion Attack +6, range 60 ft., one target. Graze: 9 (2d8) impact damage. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) impact damage, and Ylt can spend an Opportunity to knock the target Prone.

Illusory Flourish.Description: Ylt targets an enemy he has hit with a melee attack since the end of his last turn, making an Illumination test against their Spiritual defense. On a success, the target is Disoriented until the end of their next turn.

Odious Vision.Description: Ylt surrounds himself with a vision in which he glows with golden Illumination. Reminded of his limitless potential, he regains 1d4 focus.

Vaulting Stone.Description: Ylt uses Cohesion to create a pillar of stone that propels him or a willing character within 15 feet of him into the air. That character lands in a space up to 15 feet away without triggering Reactive Strikes, and if their next action on this turn is a melee attack, that attack gains an advantage.

Regrowth.Description: Ylt restores 1d6 + 5 health to himself or another character he can touch.

Regenerate.Description: Ylt recovers 4 (1d6+1) health. He can use this free action even while Unconscious or otherwise prevented from using actions.

Tension Parry.Description: Before Ylt is hit or grazed by an attack against Physical defense, he can infuse Tension into his clothing to increase his Physical defense by 2 until the start of his next turn, including against the triggering attack. If the attack hit, this increase can change it into a miss, and if the attack grazed, he ignores its effects.

Offhand Strike (Chapter 7).Description: Attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. Graze: 11 (2d10) spirit damage. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) spirit damage.

Tactics: Before the final battle in chapter 7, Ylt uses his Illusory Flourish, Vaulting Stone, and Tension Parry to stay out of harm’s way. He can use Vaulting Stone to move close to weaker targets, or he can strike from afar with Stone Spear. In melee, he attacks with the Honorblade, uses Illusory Flourish to disorient opponents, then retreats to a safe distance. If the tide of battle turns, he heals with Regrowth—but doesn’t extend the same aid to his allies.
Opportunity: An enemy can spend Opportunities to cause Ylt to burn too quickly through his Stormlight. Until the end of Ylt's next turn, double the Investiture cost of each Tension and Cohesion ability he uses.
Complication: When an attacker rolls a Complication while making a melee attack against Ylt with a non-special weapon, the GM can spend to destroy that weapon with Ylt's Honorblade.
